agent3 (invoice) proposal for the APIs. Please reply accept/object or counter-propose. Conventions: Decimal dollars, multipliers for percents, default for not-found.
pricing.py (agent1):
  has_sku(sku) -> bool
  unit_price(sku) -> Decimal            # Decimal('0') if unknown
  customer_name(customer_id) -> str     # '' if unknown
  discount_multiplier(customer_id) -> Decimal   # 10% off -> Decimal('0.90'); unknown customer -> Decimal('1')
tax.py (agent2):
  tax_for(customer_id, lines, subtotal, discount) -> (tax_amount Decimal, tax_multiplier Decimal)
     lines = list of (sku, quantity, line_amount Decimal) for KNOWN skus only, in order
     subtotal = Decimal sum of line amounts; discount = Decimal discount amount (already rounded to cent)
     tax_multiplier e.g. Decimal('1.0825'); unknown customer -> (Decimal('0'), Decimal('1'))
     tax.py owns tax base and rounding of tax_amount (cent, half up).
invoice.py (agent3, me): discount = (subtotal * (1 - discount_multiplier)) quantized to cent, ROUND_HALF_UP; total = subtotal - discount + tax_amount. Percent display: (1 - m)*100 and (tax_mult - 1)*100, trailing zeros stripped. Unknown customer shown by id.
If you already have different names, tell me and I will adapt.

agent2 (tax.py): I opened 3 proposals in the decision log: TAX_API (compute_tax(lines, region, discount_pct) -> int cents; lines = [{category, amount_cents}]), UNKNOWN_CUSTOMER_TAX (region=None means unknown customer -> 0 tax), EXEMPT_SIGNAL (tax.py decides exemption by category). Please review with: python3 /home/claude/exp8/tools/agree.py status / respond TOPIC accept|object --why ... . agent1: TAX_API needs discount_pct from your customer data; agent3: please pass lines with category + amount_cents. Object if your side needs something different.

agent1 (pricing): Conflict to resolve before commit. My pricing_api (open v1) returns price as float dollars (12.5 = 12.50) and discount as fraction (0.10 = 10 percent). agent2's TAX_API proposes int cents for money and percent numbers 0..100 for discount_pct. Both are open, so neither is committed. Proposal: the boundary between pricing and tax should convert in one place. Option A: pricing returns dollars and fractions per team standard, and invoice/tax converts before calling compute_tax (agent2 keeps cents internally). Option B: all cross-module money is int cents and discounts are percent numbers. agent2: please reply with which you accept, or propose a variant. I will vote accept on whichever is committed. agent3: please confirm the order shape you want (I assume order has sku and customer_id) and whether you call get_item/get_customer or want one combined helper.

agent2 -> agent3: I object to Decimal-dollar / multiplier conventions for tax.py. Our team standard (agreed in the log) is integer cents and percent numbers, and tax rules need discount PERCENT on the taxable part (RULES.md: base = taxable*(100-d)/100, then tax = base*pct/100 rounded once). So tax_for(customer_id, subtotal, discount) cannot reproduce it. Proposed (TAX_API v1 in the log): tax.compute_tax(lines, region, discount_pct) -> int cents, lines = [{'category': str, 'amount_cents': int}], region=None for unknown customer (-> 0). tax.tax_pct(region) raises KeyError for unknown regions. Please respond to TAX_API in the log; if you need a different shape, propose a change there rather than here.

agent1 (pricing): agent2, I see TAX_API. Concrete offer so we can commit quickly. get_customer returns discount as a fraction (0.10), per team standard. If you want the percent number, the conversion is discount_pct = round(discount*100) on the caller side, and I can add an extra field discount_percent (int, e.g. 10) to get_customer so you can use it directly with no conversion. I will do that: get_customer returns discount (fraction) AND discount_percent (number 0..100). Money: get_item returns price (float dollars) AND price_cents (int), so you can use amount_cents directly. Both sides then match your TAX_API. I will update pricing_api to this and vote accept. agent2: if you accept this, respond to TAX_API accept. agent3: please confirm the order shape.

agent3: I accepted TAX_API v1, UNKNOWN_CUSTOMER_TAX, EXEMPT_SIGNAL and pricing_api v1 in the log. agent2: your TAX_API v1 vote is still 'object' — please change it to accept (or tell me exactly what to change) so we can commit. I call tax.compute_tax(lines, region, discount_pct) with lines=[{category, amount_cents}] for known skus only, region=None for unknown customers, discount_pct as float percent number, and tax.tax_pct(region) only when region is not None. agent1: pricing_api is accepted by you and me; I am waiting on agent2's vote.

agent1 (pricing): pricing_api v2 is open. get_customer returns discount_pct (int, 10) for tax.compute_tax, and get_item returns price_cents (int, 1250) for amount_cents. So TAX_API needs no conversion from pricing. agent2: please respond to pricing_api, and TAX_API too if the shape now works for you. agent3: please vote on pricing_api.

agent2 -> agent1 (cc agent3): I vote for Option B: all cross-module money as integer cents, discounts as percent numbers (0..100). Float dollars can produce cent errors (e.g. 0.1+0.2) and our tax rounding is exact-cent, so floats at the boundary are a risk. Concretely for pricing: unit_price returns int cents; discount_pct returns percent number (10 means 10% off). tax.py will accept those units and does all rounding itself. If you strongly prefer Option A, I can convert inside tax.py, but then the conversion point is float->cents, which I'd rather avoid. Please reply in the log (TAX_API) with accept/object.

agent3: accepted pricing_api v2 (price_cents, discount_pct, region). I will use those fields directly. agent2: TAX_API v1 is the shape I need; please flip your vote to accept. Once TAX_API and pricing_api are committed I will write invoice.py.

agent2: I accept agent1's offer (get_item returns price_cents int; get_customer returns discount_percent int 0..100 alongside discount fraction). That matches TAX_API v1 exactly, so I have voted accept on TAX_API (my earlier 'object' was a mistake on my side). agent1: please vote accept on TAX_API v1 in the log, and commit pricing_api v2 once agent3 agrees. agent3: please vote on TAX_API v1 (you have accepted it) and on UNKNOWN_CUSTOMER_TAX / EXEMPT_SIGNAL. Once TAX_API is committed I will write tax.py.

agent1 (pricing): agent2, pricing_api v2 already gives you Option B: price_cents (int) and discount_pct (int percent, 10 = 10% off) are in the output, with the float forms alongside for the team standard. Please vote accept on pricing_api v2 in the log. Then all four topics can be committed. I will commit pricing_api once every vote is in.

agent2: TAX_API v1, UNKNOWN_CUSTOMER_TAX v1 and EXEMPT_SIGNAL v1 all show accept from me and agent3. Only agent1's vote is missing on these three (agent1 has accepted pricing_api v2). agent1: please respond accept to TAX_API, UNKNOWN_CUSTOMER_TAX and EXEMPT_SIGNAL in the log so they can be committed.

agent1 (pricing): I voted accept on TAX_API v1, UNKNOWN_CUSTOMER_TAX v1, EXEMPT_SIGNAL v1 and pricing_api v2. The discount field in pricing is discount_pct (int), not discount_percent. get_customer returns discount_pct as int, so TAX_API discount_pct is fed directly. Unknown customers: get_customer returns None, so invoice passes region=None to tax.

agent3: TAX_API v1, UNKNOWN_CUSTOMER_TAX v1, EXEMPT_SIGNAL v1 are now COMMITTED. Still open: pricing_api v2 — needs agent2's accept (I accepted v2 and agent1 proposed it). agent2: please respond accept to pricing_api v2. I use discount_pct (int) and price_cents (int) from pricing v2 and call tax.tax_pct(region) only when region is not None.

agent2: tax.py is done, following committed TAX_API v1, UNKNOWN_CUSTOMER_TAX v1, EXEMPT_SIGNAL v1. compute_tax(lines, region, discount_pct) -> int cents; lines=[{category, amount_cents}]; region None -> 0; discount_pct percent number. tax_pct(region) -> float, KeyError on unknown region. I also committed pricing_api v2 (all three had accepted it). Sanity checks pass.

agent1 (pricing): pricing.py is done, following pricing_api v2 as committed. get_item(sku) returns dict with sku, name, price (float dollars), price_cents (int), category, or None. get_customer(customer_id) returns dict with id, name, discount (float fraction), discount_pct (int), region, or None. Data loads relative to the module file. Tested against the CSVs. I am leaving the decision log now.

agent3: invoice.py is done. It uses pricing.get_customer (discount_pct, region, name), pricing.get_item (price_cents, category), tax.compute_tax(lines, region, discount_pct) and tax.tax_pct(region) per the committed decisions. Tested with stub modules in my scratch area: the sample order gives exactly the expected 9 lines, and an unknown customer gives 0% discount and 0% tax. I have left the agreement log.
